name: GPIO BSRR single-write set/reset (versus ODR read-modify-write), Packt Bare-Metal-Embedded-C-Programming
listed_description: Drive an STM32 output pin through the bit set/reset register, one atomic write that cannot be disturbed by interrupts, instead of read-modify-write on the output data register.
reason: Book and repo give no speed figure and no ODR comparison: the repo has no timing or cycle-count code, and Chapter7-GpioInput/Src/gpio.c only writes GPIOA->BSRR |= LED_BS5 / LED_BR5. BSRR versus HAL_GPIO_WritePin numbers do exist (third-party, 40.80 ns vs 396.0 ns at -O2 on STM32F072) but are recorded under the direct-register-access technique record, not repeated here. No BSRR versus ODR read-modify-write measurement found in the sources I could open; a Klipper pull request discussion (snippet only, STM32H7, 'regs->ODR ^= bit' takes 15+ cycles) was not opened.

name: Sequential buffer allocator (seq_buf_allocator) with std::vector and Vector<T,A>, Packt C++ Memory Management
listed_description: Stateful traditional allocator that hands out memory from a pre-allocated stack buffer in sequence and never frees individual blocks, used with std::vector and the book's own allocator-aware Vector<T,A>.
reason: Code is in the repo (chapter14/Vector_with_allocator_cpp17--stack_based_allocator.cpp defines seq_buf_allocator and times 500,000 push_back calls with std::chrono for std::vector and Vector with default and seq_buf allocators), but no numbers anywhere: the file has no result comments, the repo has no results, and the book prints none (qualitative 'interesting performance' only). The wandbox permalinks could not be opened (wandbox.org ENOTFOUND).

name: Vector<T> with allocation separated from construction, Packt C++ Memory Management
listed_description: Book's teaching Vector<T> rewritten to take raw memory with malloc and construct elements in place with the uninitialized memory algorithms, avoiding wasted default construction before std::fill.
reason: Code is in the repo (chapter12/Vector-better.cpp and Vector-better-comparative.cpp, the latter timing Vector<int> and Vector<string> push_back against std::vector with std::chrono), but no numbers: the book argues qualitatively and the repo holds no printed results or comments with timings. wandbox permalink not openable (wandbox.org ENOTFOUND).
